<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[Taliban]] insurgents ambush an [[Afghan National Army]] [[Security checkpoint|checkpoint]], killing 15 members of the security forces. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attack/taliban-kill-15-in-attack-on-afghan-security-checkpoint-local-officials-idUSKBN1YS0K2 (Reuters)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]]
**The [[Syrian Army]] continues its offensive in southern [[Idlib Governorate]] towards the key rebel-held city of [[Ma'arrat al-Nu'man]], capturing several towns and villages, including [[Jarjnaz]] and [[Sarman]]. Around 30,000 [[civilian]]s have fled the area in recent days, according to the [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/syria-regime-forces-surround-turkish-army-post-in-idlib--12207822 (Channel News Asia)]
**A war monitor reports that eight people—including five children—were killed after a missile struck a school in [[Jobas]], [[Idlib District]], used as a shelter for displaced civilians. Opposition activists blame [[Russia]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/12/children-killed-syria-missile-hits-school-191224115623082.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Arbinda attack]], [[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Maghreb insurgency]]
**Thirty-five civilians are dead and six others are injured after [[jihadists]] stormed the town of [[Arbinda]], [[Soum Province]], [[Burkina Faso]], and its military base, killing seven [[Burkina Faso Armed Forces|soldiers]]. Eighty militants were also killed. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-50908880 (BBC News)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**Gunmen attack the Christian village of [[Chibok]] in [[Borno State]], [[Nigeria]], killing seven [[Christianity in Nigeria|Christians]]. It is believed the attack was targeted for [[Christmas]]. [https://www.voanews.com/africa/7-killed-nigeria-jihadist-attack-christmas-eve (VOA News)] 

;Disasters and accidents
*A bus plunges into a [[ravine]] in [[South Sumatra]], [[Indonesia]], killing at least 25 people. [https://news.sky.com/story/sumatra-bus-crash-25-killed-after-262ft-ravine-plunge-11894592 (Sky News)]
*At least 28 people are killed after the [[Typhoon Phanfone (2019)|Typhoon Phanfone]] battered the [[Philippines]]. It led to the evacuation of more than 58,000 people. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-50921944 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[United States–Zambia relations]], [[LGBT rights in Zambia]]
**Sources report that the [[United States|U.S.]] has recalled its [[United States Ambassador to Zambia|ambassador to Zambia]] after a row over a conviction of men who were sentenced to prison in [[Zambia]] for consensual [[gay sexual practices|homosexual acts]]. [[President of Zambia]] [[Edgar Lungu]] declared ambassador [[Daniel Lewis Foote]] ''[[persona non grata]]'' because he had criticized the verdict while accusing Zambia of not actively prosecuting misappropriation of [[aid|donor aid]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-50901537 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Iraqi protests]]
**The [[Council of Representatives of Iraq|Council of Representatives]] passes a series of electoral laws to placate protestors. The laws will allow voters to [[Single-member district|select individuals]] rather than use [[Party-list proportional representation|party lists]], and the candidates will represent [[electoral district]]s rather than [[Governorates of Iraq|provinces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-protests/iraq-passes-electoral-reforms-but-deadlock-remains-idUSKBN1YS157?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Thousands of [[Ethiopia]]n [[Islam in Ethiopia|Muslims]] march across the country in response to attacks last Friday that saw four [[mosque]]s and multiple Muslim-owned businesses burned in the [[Amhara Region]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/12/ethiopian-muslims-protest-mosques-burned-191224141944689.html (Al Jazeera)]
